She was in great form (= happy and cheerful and full of energy) at the wedding party.

senses.definition: the usual way of doing something

examples.x: What's the form when you apply for a research grant?
conventional social forms
True to form (= as he usually does) he arrived an hour late.
Partners of employees are invited as a matter of form (= because that is the usual way things are done).

senses.definition: the way of doing things that is socially acceptable/not socially acceptable

examples.x: When I was a boy it was always considered bad form to talk about food or money.
Good form dictated that she should dress more casually in the country.

senses.definition: a class in a school

examples.x: Who's your form teacher?

senses.definition: a student in the form mentioned at school

examples.x: a third-former

senses.definition: of any type

examples.x: I don't approve of violence in any shape or form.
I can't stand insects in any shape or form.
I do not condone bullying in any way, shape or form.

senses.definition: to gradually form into a particular shape; to gradually develop

examples.x: In her body a new life was taking form.
